# Introduction

In this assignment, we will be analyzing and creating models from data in the [Seoul Bike Sharing Demand](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/560/seoul+bike+sharing+demand) data set. 

## Reading the data

The first thing we'll do is create a tibble out of provided the data. 

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# Load the tidyverse, ggplot and save the data to a tibble
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

#Create data tibble

bike_demand<-read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv",locale=locale(encoding="latin1"))

bike_demand
```

Note that the `locale=locale(encoding="latin1")` argument (used to fix the error mentioned in the assignment document) was found on Stack Overflow, via Google.

#EDA

## Checking the Data

### 1. 
Now that we have a tibble, the next thing we'll do is check to see if there are any missing data. To do that, we visually inspect all 8,760 rows of the tibble. Just kidding, we'll use the `is.na()` function to check that and then sum it by column, to see how many missing values we are dealing with. 

```{r}
colSums(is.na(bike_demand))
```

Zero's across the board, which is great!
